Source note: 89 FR 30136, Apr. 22, 2024, as amended at 89 FR 79732, Oct. 1, 2024.

Modified Total Direct Cost (MTDC): all direct salaries and wages, applicable fringe benefits, materials and supplies, services, travel, and up to the first $50,000 of each subaward (regardless of the period of performance of the subawards under the award).

MTDC excludes equipment, capital expenditures, charges for patient care, rental costs, tuition remission, scholarships and fellowships, participant support costs, and the portion of each subaward in excess of $50,000.

Equipment: tangible personal property (including information technology systems) with a useful life of more than one year and a per-unit acquisition cost that equals or exceeds the lesser of the capitalization level established by the recipient or subrecipient for financial statement purposes, or $10,000.
Supply: a computing device is a supply if the acquisition cost is below the lesser of the capitalization level or $10,000.

Micro-purchase threshold: the dollar amount at or below which a recipient or subrecipient may purchase property or services using micro-purchase procedures (see 200.320); no dollar figure is printed in the definition; as returned, the definitions refer to the FAR at 48 CFR part 2, subpart 2.1, and to a higher threshold approved by the cognizant agency for indirect costs.

Simplified acquisition threshold: the dollar amount below which a recipient or subrecipient may purchase property or services using small purchase methods (see 200.320); the threshold set in the FAR at 48 CFR part 2, subpart 2.1 is used; the recipient or subrecipient determines an appropriate threshold that is less than or equal to the FAR value; no dollar figure is printed.

Subaward: an award provided by a pass-through entity to a subrecipient for the subrecipient to contribute to the goals and objectives of the project by carrying out part of a Federal award received by the pass-through entity.
Fixed amount award: a type of grant or cooperative agreement under which the Federal agency or pass-through entity provides a specific amount of funding without regard to actual costs incurred.

key_facts: Proposed regulatory text, instruction 87, 200.340(a): "The Federal award may be terminated in part or its entirety as follows", with (1) "For noncompliance by the recipient or subrecipient", including a failure of the recipient to report subawards.
Proposed 200.340(a)(2) ends: "... Federal agency priorities, or the national interest as they exist at the time of the termination. See also § 200.341".

Proposed 200.340(a)(3): "By mutual agreement of the parties": termination with the consent of the recipient or subrecipient, the two parties agreeing the termination conditions, including the effective date and, for a partial termination, the portion terminated.
Proposed 200.340(a)(4) begins "Upon notification by".

Proposed 200.211(c)(1)(v): the agency must always include the termination provisions in 200.340(a)(1) through (4) in each award or incorporate them by reference, except as provided in 200.340(b); under 200.340(a)(5) it must also inform recipients of any additional termination provisions.

Preamble on 200.340: the reasons for termination are noncompliance, discretionary termination, mutual agreement, notification by the recipient or subrecipient, and additional terms and conditions in the award; sub-headings are added for each.
Preamble on 200.340: a new paragraph (d) on temporary suspension would let agencies and pass-through entities give a written order to stop work, similar to a parallel provision in the FAR.
Proposed 200.211(b)(16): the award must show the indirect cost rate, including whether the de minimis rate is charged per 200.414.

Proposed 200.339(a): the agency or pass-through entity may implement specific conditions if the recipient or subrecipient fails to comply with the U.S. Constitution, Federal statutes, regulations, or terms and conditions of the Federal award.

Proposed 200.218 regulatory text: Federal awards are not to be used in support of disparate-impact studies, disparate-impact litigation or related activities unless expressly required by law; agencies are not to adopt terms and conditions that promote or include the use of disparate-impact liability.
Preamble on new 200.219, "Prohibition of Discriminatory Event Services": the provision concerns public entities that are a recipient or subrecipient of Federal financial assistance.

Preamble on 200.205, "Federal Agency Review of Merit of Proposals": OMB proposes to strengthen requirements for merit review and to establish a new pre-issuance review process consistent with Executive Order 14332.

Part XI, "Proposed Effective Date and Length of Comment Period": OMB proposes a final rule effective by October 1, 2026 so that only a single set of government-wide requirements applies to Federal awards made during fiscal year 2027.

Preamble on part 170: OMB proposes revisions to reflect that, as of March 8, 2025, FSRS.gov was retired and all subaward reporting data and functionality are on SAM.gov; certain references to FSRS are replaced with references to SAM.gov.

Proposed Appendix A to part 25 would define System for Award Management (SAM.gov) as the Federal repository into which a recipient must provide the information required for the conduct of business as a recipient.
